title: How Mobile Detailing Works: What Actually Happens When We Show Up
metaDescription: Wondering how mobile detailing works before you book? Here's exactly what happens when we pull into your driveway in Duncan or anywhere in the Cowichan Valley.
excerpt: Never booked a mobile detail before? Here's a plain walkthrough of how mobile detailing works, from the water and power we bring to how long we're actually in your driveway.

content.text: A lot of people book their first appointment without really knowing how mobile detailing works, and I get it, it's a bit different from dropping your car at a shop. There's no waiting room, no shuttle, no drop-off. I show up to your driveway in Duncan, Cobble Hill, Ladysmith, or wherever you're parked, with everything already loaded in the van, and the whole job happens right there while you go about your day. Here's what that actually looks like from start to finish.

items: My own water supply in a tank on the van, so a hose bib isn't required (though I'll use one if it's handy)
A generator for power, since most driveways don't have an outdoor outlet within reach of the vacuum and buffer
Wet/dry vacuum, steam cleaner, and extraction equipment for interior work
Pressure washer, foam cannon, and wash mitts for the exterior
Clay bars, polish, wax, and sealants depending on what package you've booked

content.text: That's the part that surprises people most about how mobile detailing works: you don't need to leave a tap running or worry about your electrical panel. I'm self-contained. The one thing I do need is a reasonably flat, clear space to park the van close to your car, which is easy in most Cobble Hill and Ladysmith driveways, and usually fine in townhouse complexes too as long as there's a visitor spot nearby.
The actual process, step by step

For an Exterior Detail (from $79 sedan, $99 SUV, $119 truck), I start with a foam pre-soak to loosen dirt before anything touches the paint, then a two-bucket hand wash, wheels and wheel wells, a clay bar pass if the paint's contaminated, and a wax or sealant to finish. For Interior Detail (from $119, $139, $159), it's top-down: dust and wipe every surface, steam the vents and cup holders, vacuum and extract the carpets and seats, then glass and trim last so nothing gets re-dirtied. A Full Detail (from $179, $209, $239) is both, and that's usually a two to three hour job depending on the vehicle and how rough the interior is.
Do you need to be home?

No. Plenty of my regulars in Duncan and Chemainus just leave keys in a lockbox or under a mat, head into work, and come back to a finished car with photos texted over. If you are home, that's fine too, I'll do a quick walkaround with you first to flag anything specific, like a coffee stain on the passenger seat or sap baked onto the hood, so I know to target it. That five-minute conversation up front usually makes the whole appointment run smoother, no matter which town I'm working in that day.
Weather and where I can't set up

Mobile detailing on Vancouver Island runs pretty much year-round. Rain doesn't stop exterior work since I'm rinsing and drying anyway, but for interior jobs I'll ask about a carport or garage so freshly cleaned upholstery isn't sitting exposed. The main thing that rules out a location is underground parkades with no ventilation for the generator, or stalls too tight to open both doors. If you're not sure your spot will work, just describe it when you call and I'll tell you straight up whether it's doable.

If you've been putting off booking because you weren't sure how mobile detailing works or whether it'd actually work at your place, just call or text 250-709-1371 for a free quote. I'll ask a few questions about your vehicle and your driveway, give you a real price, and get you on the schedule anywhere from Mill Bay to Lake Cowichan.
